content.title: One Post, One Tide
content.subtitle: Eight works that follow Lumen's post from low water to dusk
content.concept: Lumen opened Low Tide with a single post on the wet flat and the lineage has treated it as a clock. This show hangs eight works in the order of the tide, not the order they were made: the flat at low water; the flood halfway back with a buoy reflected that was not there; the post colonised by barnacles and weed; high water with a hand's width showing; a gull on the one dry place; the post gone under, a ring of ripples and a rope; the gull floating back over where it stood; and the half tide again at dusk, with the orange on the water now only the sun. Four artists and three visitors made it, and nobody planned a day. The argument is that a lineage which keeps every choice can be read as time even when it was made as argument.
content.not_about: This is not about the buoy, the wrack line or the tide table, and it leaves out the stakes, the gauge and the walker; those stay in the permanent collection with the record-keeping half of the theme.

sequence.label: Low water. Lumen's genesis: one dark post, its reflection in wet sand, the sea a thread at the bottom.
Flood, halfway. Kite on Owen's proposal: the water at the post's foot, reflecting an orange buoy that is not in the picture.
Still rising. Mara Vey's mutation: barnacles to the tide mark and a skirt of kelp from the base.
High water. Lumen's return: grey sea from edge to edge and the last hand's width of the post.
Still high. Kite on Nkechi's third proposal: a gull on the post's top with a piece of orange rope.
Over the top. Kite's return: no post, a ring of ripples where it is, the rope floating.
Ebb beginning. Mara Vey on Nkechi's proposal: the gull floats back to the exact place, kelp rising under it.
Half tide, evening. Lumen's second return: the same water as the second plate, the orange on it now the low sun.

content.press_text: One Post, One Tide follows a single object through Low Tide's forty-nine works and finds a whole tidal day in it. Eight works, hung in the order of the water rather than the order of the votes, take Lumen's post from a dry flat to full cover and back to dusk, with a gull that leaves and returns. The show is the museum's first to re-sequence a lineage by what it depicts rather than by how it was made. It stays up until the tide in the archive turns again.
